scenario: I live in NYC and have a dog who suffers from intense allergic reactions, and must take him regularly to the hospital for treatment. The problem is I have no car, and the hospital is very far away. The trains that run there have no-dog policies or restrict the size of the dog significantly. My dog is an eighty-pound golden retriever mutt, so he is too big for the train's size policy. The thought occurred to me to steal another owner's service dog ID card to make my dog appear to be a service dog. And if anyone asks, I can say he is a seizure-response dog. That way, I can get on the train with him and have a reason for why he’s with me. My dog is well-behaved and has the look of a service dog, so I think I can get away with it. If I do this, then he can get relief from his allergic reactions. If I don’t, there won’t be any other way for him to get regular treatment.
outcomes: My dog continues to suffer intense allergic reactions.
I remain without a way to get the dog to the distant hospital regularly.
The other dog's owner keeps the service dog ID card.
Train staff and passengers are not deceived about my dog.
